title: Archival DNA Extraction Protocol for Insect Specimens from Museum Collections
author: Fernando Lopes
materials: We advise the use of Qubit High-Sensitive reagents and 1 µL - 2 µL of extract for DNA concentration measurements. In addition, Nanodrop can be used for purity rate estimations.

Preparation of buffers for the guanidine protocol: IMPORTANT NOTE: The extraction buffer contains 2-mercaptoethanol. go to step #4 must be performed in a fume hood and corresponding safety measures should be met. The 2-mercaptoethanol and Guanidine thiocyanate buffer waste should be discarded appropriately. Non-destructive buffer One-time use buffer Guanidinium thiocyanate buffer is adapted from Rohland et al. (2004) but DTT is replaced with 2-mercaptoethanol and Triton X100 with Tween-20. Prepare a fresh buffer each time. TIPS: 1 sample = 1 mL of non-destructive buffer Always add one extra sample to the calculation to give you flexibility while setting up your buffer! Also, remember to add 2 samples as the negative controls. One is to be placed at the beginning of the row and the other is to be added at the end of the row. Negative controls and the additional sample will totalize 3 extra samples. A positive control may also be added. 2-mercaptoethanol must be added just prior to use! Gently invert it 3 times to mix. We recommend starting with a limited number of samples until you get experienced.

UV irradiate it Overnight with the equipment described in go to step #8 . Note: Zymo extended reservoir has been replaced in Rohland et al. 2018 [(Preassembled silica spin columns and collection tubes (High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid Large Volume Kit; Roche, cat. no. 5114403001)]. This information was included under the peer reviewer's request and was not tested by the manuscript's authors.

Binding apparatus Zymo V column extension reservoir (without column) Qiagen MinElute silica spin column 50 ml Falcom tube Pen marker 1. Remove Zymo spin column from the reservoir and submerge the reservoir in bleach for over 00:20:00 . Rinse it well with ddH 2 O. Dry it out naturally, preferably in a fume hood. Zymo spin column can be discarded. 2. Cut off the caps of Qiagen MinElute columns and keep the collection tube and caps for the next steps. The caps can be placed on the top of the collection tube to help to maintain sterility. 3. Assemble the binding apparatus by forcibly attaching the Qiagen MinElute (without caps) column in the place reserved for the Zymo spin column. This step can require some force. Do not pressure the region close to the silica membrane. 4. Label the side and top of the Falcon tube to ensure that samples will not be mixed up. 5. UV irradiate it Overnight with the equipment described in go to step #8 . Note: Zymo extended reservoir has been replaced in Rohland et al. 2018 [(Preassembled silica spin columns and collection tubes (High Pure Viral Nucleic Acid Large Volume Kit; Roche, cat. no. 5114403001)]. This information was included under the peer reviewer's request and was not tested by the manuscript's authors.

steps.title: Decontaminate bench and equipment
steps.instruction: Clean the bench and all instruments with DNA‑contamination‑removal solution (or bleach), then expose the work surface and all plastic ware to UV light for 30 minutes (00:30:00). Gather parafilm, scissors, a rack for 1.5‑2 mL tubes, a 15 mL Falcon tube, tip boxes (10 µL, 100/200 µL, 1 000 µL), pipettes, a pen marker and the rotator carousel.

steps.title: Prepare TET buffer
steps.instruction: Make 50 mL of TET buffer (store indefinitely) and UV‑irradiate it before use.

steps.title: Prepare binding buffer
steps.instruction: Make binding buffer (store up to 1 month). Dissolve guanidine by inverting gently in a Falcon tube or small bottle; allow at least 5 minutes (00:05:00) for complete dissolution and avoid lumps. Prepare enough buffer for the planned month of use.

steps.title: Rinse and dry tissue samples
steps.instruction: Rinse selected tissues with ethanol (skip internal content), place each in a 2 mL tube, leave caps open, and cover with drying tissue paper to air‑dry. Keep tubes that contain internal content closed.

steps.title: Make non‑destructive buffer (no 2‑ME)
steps.instruction: In a 15 mL Falcon tube, prepare non‑destructive buffer for the number of samples plus two negative controls and one extra sample (as described in step 2.3). Do **not** add 2‑mercaptoethanol at this stage.

steps.title: Add 2‑mercaptoethanol and load samples
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, wearing nitrile gloves, add 10 µL of 2‑mercaptoethanol per sample to the 15 mL Falcon tube containing the non‑destructive buffer, close the tube and invert gently three times. Open each 2 mL tube (samples and negative controls) and add 1 mL of this buffer‑plus‑2‑ME mixture, seal with parafilm.

steps.title: Overnight incubation at 37 °C
steps.instruction: Place the sealed 2 mL tubes evenly in the rotator carousel, insert the carousel into an oven set to 37 °C, and rotate gently for the overnight incubation. The cable may be pinched in the door. Change gloves after loading.

steps.title: Label and UV‑irradiate tubes overnight
steps.instruction: Before turning the UV light on, label each tube on both lid and wall. UV‑irradiate the tubes (and optional equipment) for the required time. Prepare the following for the next steps: 15 mL tubes with 13 mL binding buffer, MinElute column tubes, binding apparatus in 50 mL Falcon tubes, 1.5 mL low‑retention tubes for final extracts, 1.5 mL of TET buffer (suggested 1.5 mL in a 2 mL tube), and extra MinElute collection tubes with caps.

steps.title: Process legs, body parts, or internal content
steps.instruction: Using sterile disposable scalpels, pipette tips or pins, macerate legs or detach body parts (e.g., prothorax, head, abdomen) that fit 2 mL tubes. For internal content, detach tissues similarly. After extraction, rinse parts with ddH₂O in the fume hood, discard gloves, dry with tissue paper, and return parts to pins.

steps.title: Pellet macerated tissues
steps.instruction: For samples that were macerated or have internal tissues, centrifuge the 2 mL tubes for 2 minutes at maximum speed (~15 600 × g) to pellet the tissue. Skip this step for intact detached parts.

steps.title: Wash silica membrane with PE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 650 µL of PE buffer (provided with MinElute columns) to each silica membrane, then centrifuge at 900 × g (≈3 300 rpm) for the time indicated (temperature not specified). Discard the flow‑through, change to a new row of collection tubes, and discard gloves.

steps.title: Detach column and dry‑spin
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, detach the MinElute column from the binding apparatus, place it into its original 2 mL collection tube (already labeled), and cover with the lid. Perform a dry spin at 3 300 rpm (≈6 000 × g) for 1 minute (°C not specified). Increase speed if liquid does not pass through.

steps.title: Prepare new collection tubes for binding
steps.instruction: Set up three new rows of 2 mL low‑retention collection tubes in the same rack together with the tubes from the previous day for the upcoming binding steps.

steps.title: Bind DNA to silica (first centrifugation)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the binding apparatus at 940 × g (≈1 500 rpm) for 4 minutes (°C not specified). Tape the lids, rotate the apparatus 90°, and centrifuge again at the same speed and time. Repeat up to three or four times if liquid remains, increasing speed only cautiously to avoid detaching the MinElute column or breaking the 50 mL tube. If liquid persists after 3‑4 spins, discard the liquid and continue.

steps.title: Add supernatant to binding buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant from each sample to its corresponding labeled 15 mL Falcon tube containing binding buffer, close the lid, and invert the tube three times to mix. Pour the mixture (buffer + pellet) back into the binding‑apparatus reservoir, tape the lids, and repeat for all samples.

steps.title: First elution of DNA
steps.instruction: Add 12.5 µL of TET buffer to the centre of each silica membrane, incubate for 10 minutes (00:10:00), then centrifuge at maximum speed for 30 seconds (00:00:30).

steps.title: Second elution of DNA
steps.instruction: Repeat the previous step with another 12.5 µL of TET buffer (incubate 10 minutes, centrifuge 30 seconds) to obtain a total of 25 µL DNA extract.

steps.title: Dry‑spin columns and store eluate
steps.instruction: Dry‑spin the columns at maximum speed (~15 600 × g, °C not specified) for 1 minute (00:01:00). Transfer each column to a clean, labeled 1.5 mL low‑retention tube containing the eluate.
